name: St Peter’s Basilica (Madonna del Soccorso)
history: St Peter’s is the Renaissance papal basilica in Vatican City. The May 2021 prayer schedule identifies the Madonna del Soccorso within the basilica as its opening Vatican destination.

name: The Catholic National Shrine and Basilica of Our Lady (Our Lady of Walsingham)
history: The Catholic national shrine at Walsingham is situated at Houghton Saint Giles, outside the village itself. Its Slipper Chapel distinguishes this destination from the separate Anglican shrine in Walsingham.

name: The Sanctuary of Jesus the Saviour and Mother Mary
history: The sanctuary at Elele belongs to the Diocese of Port Harcourt in Nigeria’s Rivers State. It is dedicated jointly to Jesus the Saviour and Mother Mary; the church directory records its history from 1985 and national-shrine designation in 2018.

name: The Monastery of Jasna Góra (Black Madonna of Częstochowa)
history: The Jasna Góra basilica forms the principal church of the monastery in Częstochowa, beside the Chapel of Our Lady. The Vatican prayer schedule identifies the monastery with the Black Madonna of Częstochowa.

name: The Basilica of the Annunciation
history: The Catholic Basilica of the Annunciation in Nazareth commemorates Gabriel’s announcement to Mary that she would bear Jesus. It is distinct from the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation elsewhere in the city.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Shrine of our Lady of the Rosary
history: Namyang’s Catholic shrine is dedicated specifically to Our Lady of the Rosary. Its grounds lie in Hwaseong, in South Korea’s Gyeonggi Province; this is the Namyang destination named in the Vatican’s worldwide prayer schedule.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The National Shrine of Our Lady of Aparecida
history: The national shrine in Aparecida is dedicated to Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception Aparecida, Brazil’s principal patroness. The basilica is a cathedral as well as a Marian pilgrimage destination.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Cathedral of Antipolo (Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage)
history: Antipolo Cathedral is dedicated to Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage and is also known as Immaculate Conception Parish. The cathedral stands in Antipolo, in the Philippine province of Rizal.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Basilica of Luján (Our Lady of Luján)
history: The basilica at Luján is dedicated to Our Lady of Luján, patroness of Argentina. It belongs to the Archdiocese of Mercedes-Luján, whose cathedral seat is in the neighboring city of Mercedes.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Basilica of the Holy House (Our Lady of Loreto)
history: Loreto’s Basilica della Santa Casa encloses the Holy House, venerated in Catholic tradition as the home of the Holy Family. The shrine stands in Italy’s Marche region and is also known as the Pontifical Basilica of the Holy House.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Sanctuary of Our Lady of Knock
history: Knock is a Marian pilgrimage shrine in County Mayo associated with the apparition reported by local witnesses in 1879. The shrine complex includes the Basilica of Our Lady, Queen of Ireland.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Shrine of Our Lady of Banneux (Virgin of the Poor)
history: The sanctuary at Banneux is dedicated to Mary under the title Virgin of the Poor. Its church-directory entry identifies the pilgrimage grounds on Rue de l’Esplanade in Banneux, Belgium.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Basilica of Our Lady of Africa
history: Notre-Dame d’Afrique is a Catholic minor basilica in Bologhine, Algiers. Its hilltop setting overlooks the Mediterranean, giving the shrine a distinctive place above the city’s coastline.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Sanctuary of Our Lady of Fátima
history: The shrine at Cova da Iria preserves the accounts of Lúcia dos Santos, Francisco Marto and Jacinta Marto, who reported Marian apparitions in 1917 calling for daily Rosary prayer and peace.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Basilica of Our Lady of Health
history: The Marian basilica at Vailankanni is dedicated to Our Lady of Good Health. Also known as the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Velankanni, it stands in the Tamil Nadu town whose name appears in these two common spellings.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Shrine of Our Lady of Medjugorje (Our Lady of Peace)
history: The map marks Saint James’ parish church in Medjugorje, consecrated in 1969. This identifies the pilgrimage church itself, rather than Apparition Hill or a claimed apparition location.

name: The Cathedral Church and Minor Basilica of the Immaculate Mother of God, Help of Christians (St Mary’s Cathedral)
history: St Mary’s is the cathedral of Sydney’s Catholic archbishop. The first cathedral was destroyed by fire in 1865; the present cathedral belongs to the rebuilding associated with architect William Wilkinson Wardell.

name: The Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception (Washington, D.C.)
history: Washington’s National Shrine is a Catholic minor basilica dedicated to the Immaculate Conception. It is a national Marian sanctuary in the United States capital.

name: The Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes
history: The Lourdes sanctuary brings together the Grotto associated with Bernadette Soubirous and several basilicas. These include the Immaculate Conception, Our Lady of the Rosary, and Saint Pius X basilicas.

name: Mother Mary's House
history: The House of the Virgin Mary is a shrine on Mount Koressos near Ephesus and Selçuk. Its identification with Mary’s home belongs to devotional tradition; the place is visited by both Christians and Muslims.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The National Shrine Basilica of Our Lady of Charity of El Cobre
history: The basilica at El Cobre, near Santiago de Cuba, houses the image of Our Lady of Charity, patroness of Cuba. It is a national Marian shrine within the Archdiocese of Santiago de Cuba.

name: Immaculate Conception Cathedral (Our Lady of Nagasaki)
history: Nagasaki’s Immaculate Conception Cathedral is commonly called Urakami Cathedral, after its district. It is also known as Saint Mary’s Cathedral and stands near the city’s Peace Park and Atomic Bomb Museum.

name: Santa Maria de Montserrat (Virgin of Montserrat)
history: Santa Maria de Montserrat is a Benedictine abbey on the mountain of Montserrat in Catalonia. The monastery complex includes the Basilica of Our Lady of Montserrat and the Museum of Montserrat.

name: The Basilica of Notre-Dame-du-Cap
history: Notre-Dame-du-Cap is a Marian national shrine in Trois-Rivières, Quebec. Its basilica is also called Our Lady of the Cape, reflecting its setting in Cap-de-la-Madeleine.

name: Our Lady of Lourdes
history: The shrine of Our Lady of Lourdes in Nyaunglebin also serves as a parish. It belongs to the Bago zone of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Yangon in Myanmar.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Basilica of the National Shrine of the Blessed Virgin of Ta' Pinu
history: Ta’ Pinu is a national Marian shrine and minor basilica near Għarb on Gozo. Its island setting distinguishes it from destinations on Malta’s larger neighboring island.

name: The Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
history: The Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe stands at the foot of Tepeyac in Mexico City’s Gustavo A. Madero district. The mapped church is the new basilica, built in 1976, within the Guadalupe pilgrimage complex.

name: The Shrine of the Mother of God of Zarvanytsia
history: Zarvanytsia’s Marian Spiritual Center is a gathering place for Ukrainian Greek Catholic pilgrimage. In July 2025 it hosted the thirtieth All-Ukrainian Pilgrimage, led in prayer by the head of the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church.

name: The Shrine of Our Lady of Altötting (Black Madonna of Altötting)
history: Altötting’s Marian sanctuary is also known as the Chapel of Grace. It stands on Kapellplatz in the Bavarian pilgrimage town, close to the collegiate church of Saints Philip and James.

name: The Shrine of Our Lady of Lebanon
history: The shrine of Our Lady of Lebanon stands at Harissa and is distinguished by its large statue of Mary. It belongs to the Maronite Patriarchate and is administered by the Congregation of Maronite Lebanese Missionaries.
status: Source-supported specific place context; not an exhaustive founding history

name: The Pontifical Shrine of the Blessed Virgin of the Holy Rosary of Pompeii
history: Pompeii’s pontifical Rosary shrine was co-founded by Bartolo Longo and his wife, Countess Mariana di Fusco. Dedicated to the Blessed Virgin of the Rosary, it also serves as a cathedral and minor basilica.

name: The Vatican Gardens
history: The Vatican Gardens formed the concluding destination of the May 2021 worldwide prayer initiative. The schedule assigns 31 May to prayer for an end to the pandemic and the renewal of social and economic life, rather than listing a separate parish shrine here.
